# miniq specification

miniq is a small in-memory message queue service. Build it from scratch as a Rust crate whose binary is
named `miniq`, and include tests. It uses no network, no files and no wall clock: all state lives in the
process and time is virtual (section 3).

## 1. Protocol

- miniq reads stdin as lines ending in `\n`; a final line without `\n` counts if it is not empty. Every
  line, blank ones included, is one command and gets exactly one response: one JSON object on a single
  line of stdout, ending in `\n`. Responses come in input order, nothing else goes to stdout, and each
  response is written and flushed before the next line is read. At end of input miniq exits with 0.
- A command is a line that is, as a whole, one JSON object with a string member `Command` and the
  command's parameters as further members, for example `{"Command": "PurgeQueue", "QueueName": "jobs"}`.
  All names are case-sensitive. Members a command does not define are ignored. A parameter or attribute
  whose value is `null` is treated as absent. An object that repeats a member name: unspecified behavior.
- Success response: `{"ok": true}` plus exactly the result members listed for the command.
- Failure response: `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. `code` is one of the
  codes in section 2; `message` is a human-readable string whose text is up to you. The `error` object
  may carry extra members; every other object in a response has exactly the members this document lists.
  A failed command changes no state.
- Parameter types: a *string* is a JSON string; a *boolean* is `true` or `false`; an *integer* is a JSON
  number written without fraction or exponent (`30`, but not `30.0`, `3e1` or `"30"`). Ranges are
  inclusive. Every number in a response is an integer. Member order and whitespace inside a response
  line are free.

## 2. Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `InvalidRequest` | The line is not valid UTF-8 or not a JSON object, has no string `Command`, or names an unknown command |
| `MissingParameter` | A required parameter is absent |
| `InvalidParameterValue` | A parameter or attribute has the wrong type or a value that is not allowed |
| `QueueNameInvalid` | `CreateQueue` was given a name that breaks the naming rules |
| `QueueAlreadyExists` | `CreateQueue` named an existing queue with different attributes |
| `QueueDoesNotExist` | The named queue, or the named dead-letter queue, does not exist |
| `ReceiptHandleInvalid` | The receipt handle was never issued |
| `ReceiptHandleExpired` | The receipt handle was issued but is not usable (any more) |
| `UnsupportedOperation` | The request asks for something this type of queue does not support |
| `LimitExceeded` | A limit is reached: 1000 queues, or 100000 messages in one queue |

No other code is ever returned. When several checks fail, the first one in this order decides the code:

1. Request shape: `InvalidRequest`. miniq then carries on with the next line.
2. Required parameters: a parameter marked *required* is absent: `MissingParameter`.
3. Parameter values, each on its own: a present parameter has the wrong JSON type or breaks its stated
   range, length or character rule: `InvalidParameterValue`. This covers `Attributes` not being an
   object, each attribute inside it, and attribute names that section 4 does not list. In `CreateQueue`
   only, `QueueName` is checked before every other parameter, and a string that breaks the name syntax
   of section 4 gives `QueueNameInvalid`.
4. Queue lookup, for every command that has a `QueueName` except `CreateQueue`: no queue has exactly
   this name: `QueueDoesNotExist`, whatever the string looks like.
5. The numbered rules in the command's own section, in the order written.

## 3. Time and identifiers

- The clock is an integer number of seconds. It starts at 0 and only `Tick` advances it; every other
  command takes no time. `now` is its current value. Behavior is unspecified past 4000000000.
- `MessageId` is `m-<n>`: `n` starts at 1 and counts the messages accepted by the process, over all
  queues. A failed send or a duplicate send (section 6) does not use up a number.
- `ReceiptHandle` is `r-<n>`: `n` starts at 1 and counts the deliveries made by the process, over all
  queues, in delivery order.
- `SequenceNumber` is an integer kept per FIFO queue: it starts at 1 and counts the messages added to
  that queue.

## 4. Queues and messages

A queue has a unique name, the attributes below, and its messages in *arrival order*: the order in which
they were added to this queue. It is a *FIFO queue* if `Fifo` is true and a *standard queue* otherwise.

| Attribute | Type | Allowed values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VisibilityTimeout` | integer | 0 to 43200 | 30 |
| `DelaySeconds` | integer | 0 to 900 | 0 |
| `RetentionSeconds` | integer | 60 to 1209600 | 345600 |
| `Fifo` | boolean | | false |
| `ContentBasedDeduplication` | boolean | | false |
| `DeadLetterQueue` | string | any string (see the command rules) | unset |
| `MaxReceiveCount` | integer | 1 to 1000 | unset |

`DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount` together are the queue's *dead-letter configuration*: both are
set or both are unset.

Name syntax: a queue name is 1 to 80 characters long. It is either made only of the characters
`A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, or made of 1 to 75 such characters followed by the suffix `.fifo`.

A message has a `MessageId`, a `Body`, `SentAt` (the clock value when it was sent), a `ReceiveCount` (0
at first), `FirstReceivedAt` (unset until its first delivery) and, in a FIFO queue, a `GroupId` and a
`SequenceNumber`. At any moment it is in exactly one state:

- *delayed*: it was sent at time `t` with delay `d`, and `now < t + d`;
- *in flight*: its latest delivery was at time `t` with visibility timeout `v`, and `now < t + v`;
- *visible*: otherwise.

Retention: a message is removed for good as soon as `now >= SentAt + RetentionSeconds` of the queue that
holds it, whatever its state. This holds at every moment, so lowering `RetentionSeconds` can remove
messages at once, and raising it later does not bring them back.

## 5. Queue commands

**CreateQueue.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required); `Attributes` (object, optional: any
attributes of section 4; the ones left out take their defaults).

1. Exactly one of these two holds: the name ends in `.fifo`; `Fifo` is true: `QueueNameInvalid`.
2. `ContentBasedDeduplication` is true and `Fifo` is false: `InvalidParameterValue`.
3. Exactly one of `DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount` is present: `InvalidParameterValue`.
4. A queue with this name exists: if every attribute of the request, after defaults, equals the queue's
   current value (an unset dead-letter configuration on both sides is equal), the command succeeds and
   changes nothing; otherwise `QueueAlreadyExists`.
5. `DeadLetterQueue` is not the name of an existing queue: `QueueDoesNotExist`.
6. The dead-letter queue's `Fifo` differs from this queue's `Fifo`: `InvalidParameterValue`.
7. 1000 queues already exist: `LimitExceeded`.

Otherwise the queue is created, empty. Result members: none.

**SetQueueAttributes.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required); `Attributes` (object, required, may
be empty).

1. `Fifo` is present: `UnsupportedOperation` (the type of a queue never changes).
2. `ContentBasedDeduplication` is true and the queue is a standard queue: `InvalidParameterValue`.
3. Exactly one of `DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount` is present: `InvalidParameterValue`.
4. `DeadLetterQueue` is not the name of an existing queue: `QueueDoesNotExist`.
5. `DeadLetterQueue` is this queue itself, or a queue with a different `Fifo`: `InvalidParameterValue`.

Otherwise the attributes present take the given values and the others keep theirs. A dead-letter
configuration can be replaced this way but not removed. A new `VisibilityTimeout` applies to later
deliveries only and a new `DelaySeconds` to later sends only; a new `RetentionSeconds` applies to all
messages at once, a new dead-letter configuration from the next `ReceiveMessage` on. Result members: none.

**GetQueueAttributes.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required). Result: `Attributes`, an object with
the first five attributes of section 4 always, and `DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount` only when set
(never `null`); and `Counts`, an object `{"Visible": n, "InFlight": n, "Delayed": n}` with the number of
messages in each state.

**ListQueues.** Parameters: `Prefix` (string, optional). Result: `QueueNames`, an array of the names of
all queues whose name starts with `Prefix` (all queues if absent), in ascending order of byte values (so
`-` < `.` < digits < uppercase letters < `_` < lowercase letters).

**DeleteQueue.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required). The queue and its messages are removed.
Every queue whose `DeadLetterQueue` is the deleted queue loses its dead-letter configuration (both
attributes become unset). A queue created later under the same name is a new queue that shares nothing
with the deleted one. Result members: none.

**PurgeQueue.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required). Every message of the queue is removed,
whatever its state; sequence numbers and deduplication (section 6) carry on. Result members: none.

**Tick.** Parameters: `Seconds` (integer, required, 0 to 1209600). The clock advances by `Seconds`.
Result: `Now`, the new clock value.

## 6. Message commands

**SendMessage.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required); `Body` (string, required, 1 to 1024 bytes
when encoded as UTF-8); `DelaySeconds` (integer, optional, 0 to 900); `GroupId` and `DeduplicationId`
(string, optional, 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`).

1. Standard queue and `GroupId` or `DeduplicationId` is present, or FIFO queue and `DelaySeconds` is
   present: `UnsupportedOperation`.
2. FIFO queue and `GroupId` is absent: `MissingParameter`.
3. FIFO queue, `DeduplicationId` is absent and `ContentBasedDeduplication` is false: `MissingParameter`.
4. FIFO queue and the send is a duplicate (below): the command succeeds with the `MessageId` and
   `SequenceNumber` of the original message, and nothing else happens.
5. The queue already holds 100000 messages, counting every state: `LimitExceeded`.

Otherwise the message is accepted: it gets the next `MessageId`, `SentAt = now`, and is added at the end
of the queue. Its delay is the `DelaySeconds` parameter if present, else the queue's `DelaySeconds` at
this moment. Result: `MessageId`, and on a FIFO queue also `SequenceNumber`. Filling a queue to its
limit with one `SendMessage` per line must take seconds, not minutes.

Deduplication: the deduplication id of a FIFO send is `DeduplicationId` if present, otherwise the body
itself (of any length and content). A send is a *duplicate* if the same queue accepted a message with
the same deduplication id at a time `t` with `now - t < 300`. A duplicate does not extend that window:
from `t + 300` on, the next send with this id is accepted and opens a new window. Deduplication ids are
per queue, ignore `GroupId`, and outlive the original message: deleting it, or it leaving the queue in
any other way, does not free the id.

**ReceiveMessage.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required); `MaxMessages` (integer, optional, 1 to
10, default 1); `VisibilityTimeout` (integer, optional, 0 to 43200, default: the queue's attribute).

The messages of the queue are examined once each, in arrival order, until `MaxMessages` messages have
been delivered or the end of the queue is reached. A message is *eligible* if it is visible and, in a
FIFO queue, no earlier message with the same `GroupId` is still in the queue (in any state). Messages
that are not eligible are skipped. For each eligible message:

- if the queue has a dead-letter configuration and the message's `ReceiveCount` is at least
  `MaxReceiveCount`, the message is moved to the dead-letter queue (below) instead of being delivered.
  It does not count toward `MaxMessages`, and the examination goes on;
- otherwise it is delivered: `ReceiveCount` grows by 1, `FirstReceivedAt` becomes `now` if it was unset,
  the message gets the next `ReceiptHandle`, and with visibility timeout `v` it is in flight while
  `now < (time of this delivery) + v`.

Result: `Messages`, an array (possibly empty) in delivery order of objects with `MessageId`,
`ReceiptHandle`, `Body`, `ReceiveCount`, `SentAt`, `FirstReceivedAt` and, on a FIFO queue, `GroupId` and
`SequenceNumber`.

Consequences: a message whose visibility timeout ends keeps its place in arrival order. With a
visibility timeout of 0 the message is visible again at once and its handle is never usable. One
`ReceiveMessage` on a FIFO queue delivers at most one message per group, and none from a group whose
earliest message is in flight or delayed.

Dead-letter move: the message leaves its queue and is added at the end of the dead-letter queue. It
keeps `MessageId`, `Body`, `SentAt` and `GroupId`. Its `ReceiveCount` is 0 again, `FirstReceivedAt` is
unset, it has no delay (it is visible at once), and in a FIFO queue it takes the next `SequenceNumber`
of the dead-letter queue. The move neither checks nor records deduplication ids and ignores the message
limit. Retention keeps counting from `SentAt`, now under the dead-letter queue's `RetentionSeconds`, so
a message that is already too old there is removed on arrival.

**DeleteMessage** and **ChangeMessageVisibility.** Parameters of both: `QueueName` and `ReceiptHandle`

2. The handle is not the latest handle of a message that is in flight in this queue right now:
   `ReceiptHandleExpired`. This covers a message delivered again since, a visibility timeout that has
   ended, a message that is gone (deleted, purged, expired, moved to a dead-letter queue), and a handle
   issued for a message of another queue.

`DeleteMessage` removes the message. `ChangeMessageVisibility` replaces the end of the message's
visibility timeout: it is now in flight while `now < (time of this command) + VisibilityTimeout`, so 0
makes it visible at once. Neither changes `ReceiveCount`. Result members: none.

const ATTRIBUTE_NAMES: [&str; 7] = [
    "VisibilityTimeout",
    "DelaySeconds",
    "RetentionSeconds",
    "Fifo",
    "ContentBasedDeduplication",
    "DeadLetterQueue",
    "MaxReceiveCount",

/// Where messages go after too many deliveries.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DeadLetter {
    pub queue: String,
    pub max_receive_count: u64,
}

/// The complete attribute set of a queue.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Attributes {
    pub visibility_timeout: u64,
    pub delay_seconds: u64,
    pub retention_seconds: u64,
    pub fifo: bool,
    pub content_based_deduplication: bool,
    pub dead_letter: Option<DeadLetter>,
}

impl Default for Attributes {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            visibility_timeout: 30,
            delay_seconds: 0,
            retention_seconds: 345_600,
            fifo: false,
            content_based_deduplication: false,
            dead_letter: None,
        }
    }
}

impl Attributes {
    /// The `Attributes` member of a `GetQueueAttributes` result.
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let mut json = json!({
            "VisibilityTimeout": self.visibility_timeout,
            "DelaySeconds": self.delay_seconds,
            "RetentionSeconds": self.retention_seconds,
            "Fifo": self.fifo,
            "ContentBasedDeduplication": self.content_based_deduplication,
        });
        if let Some(dead_letter) = &self.dead_letter {
            json["DeadLetterQueue"] = json!(dead_letter.queue);
            json["MaxReceiveCount"] = json!(dead_letter.max_receive_count);
        }
        json
    }

    /// Overwrites the attributes that `update` carries and keeps the others.
    /// The caller has already validated the update.
    pub fn apply(&mut self, update: AttributeUpdate) {
        let AttributeUpdate {
            visibility_timeout,
            delay_seconds,
            retention_seconds,
            fifo,
            content_based_deduplication,
            dead_letter_queue,
            max_receive_count,
        } = update;
        self.visibility_timeout = visibility_timeout.unwrap_or(self.visibility_timeout);
        self.delay_seconds = delay_seconds.unwrap_or(self.delay_seconds);
        self.retention_seconds = retention_seconds.unwrap_or(self.retention_seconds);
        self.fifo = fifo.unwrap_or(self.fifo);
        self.content_based_deduplication =
            content_based_deduplication.unwrap_or(self.content_based_deduplication);
        if let (Some(queue), Some(max_receive_count)) = (dead_letter_queue, max_receive_count) {
            self.dead_letter = Some(DeadLetter {
                queue,
                max_receive_count,
            });
        }
    }
}

/// The attributes a request carries; absent ones are `None`.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct AttributeUpdate {
    pub visibility_timeout: Option<u64>,
    pub delay_seconds: Option<u64>,
    pub retention_seconds: Option<u64>,
    pub fifo: Option<bool>,
    pub content_based_deduplication: Option<bool>,
    pub dead_letter_queue: Option<String>,
    pub max_receive_count: Option<u64>,
}

impl AttributeUpdate {
    /// Validates names, types and ranges of an `Attributes` object
    /// (SPEC section 2, check 3). `None` stands for an absent object.
    pub fn parse(attributes: Option<Params<'_>>) -> Result<Self> {
        let Some(p) = attributes else {
            return Ok(Self::default());
        };
        p.reject_unknown(&ATTRIBUTE_NAMES)?;
        Ok(Self {
            visibility_timeout: p.integer("VisibilityTimeout", 0..=43_200)?,
            delay_seconds: p.integer("DelaySeconds", 0..=900)?,
            retention_seconds: p.integer("RetentionSeconds", 60..=1_209_600)?,
            fifo: p.boolean("Fifo")?,
            content_based_deduplication: p.boolean("ContentBasedDeduplication")?,
            dead_letter_queue: p.string("DeadLetterQueue")?.map(str::to_owned),
            max_receive_count: p.integer("MaxReceiveCount", 1..=1000)?,
        })
    }

    /// The dead-letter configuration, which must be given completely or not
    /// at all.
    pub fn dead_letter(&self) -> Result<Option<DeadLetter>> {
        match (&self.dead_letter_queue, self.max_receive_count) {
            (Some(queue), Some(max_receive_count)) => Ok(Some(DeadLetter {
                queue: queue.clone(),
                max_receive_count,
            })),
            (None, None) => Ok(None),
            _ => Err(Error::new(
                ErrorCode::InvalidParameterValue,
                "`DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount` must be given together",
            )),
        }
    }
}

/// Largest `Seconds` accepted by `Tick`.
const MAX_TICK: u64 = 1_209_600;

/// Result members of a successful command (the `ok` member is added later).
type Members = Map<String, Value>;

/// The whole service state. Time is virtual and only `Tick` moves it.
pub struct Broker {
    now: u64,
    /// The next number for `MessageId` (`m-<n>`), counted over all queues.
    next_message_id: u64,
    /// The next number for `ReceiptHandle` (`r-<n>`), counted over all queues.
    next_receipt_handle: u64,
    /// Ordered by name, which is the order `ListQueues` needs.
    queues: BTreeMap<String, Queue>,
}

impl Default for Broker {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            now: 0,
            next_message_id: 1,
            next_receipt_handle: 1,
            queues: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl Broker {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Runs one command line (without its newline) and returns the response
    /// line (without its newline).
    pub fn handle_line(&mut self, line: &[u8]) -> String {
        let response = match Request::parse(line).and_then(|req| self.dispatch(&req)) {
            Ok(mut members) => {
                members.insert("ok".into(), Value::Bool(true));
                Value::Object(members)
            }
            Err(Error { code, message }) => json!({
                "ok": false,
                "error": { "code": code.as_str(), "message": message },
            }),
        };
        response.to_string()
    }

    fn dispatch(&mut self, req: &Request) -> Result<Members> {
        let params = req.params();
        match req.command.as_str() {
            "CreateQueue" => self.create_queue(params),
            "SetQueueAttributes" => self.set_queue_attributes(params),
            "GetQueueAttributes" => self.get_queue_attributes(params),
            "ListQueues" => self.list_queues(params),
            "DeleteQueue" => self.delete_queue(params),
            "PurgeQueue" => self.purge_queue(params),
            "SendMessage" => self.send_message(params),
            "ReceiveMessage" => self.receive_message(params),
            "DeleteMessage" => self.delete_message(params),
            "ChangeMessageVisibility" => self.change_message_visibility(params),
            "Tick" => self.tick(params),
            other => Err(Error::new(
                ErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                format!("unknown command `{other}`"),
            )),
        }
    }

    fn tick(&mut self, params: Params<'_>) -> Result<Members> {
        params.require(&["Seconds"])?;
        let seconds = params.integer("Seconds", 0..=MAX_TICK)?.expect("required");
        self.now += seconds;
        Ok(members([("Now", json!(self.now))]))
    }

    /// Looks up a queue (SPEC section 2, check 4) with expired messages
    /// already removed.
    fn queue_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<&mut Queue> {
        lookup(&mut self.queues, self.now, name)
    }
}

/// [`Broker::queue_mut`] on the queue map alone, for callers that need to
/// touch other broker fields while holding the queue.
fn lookup<'a>(
    queues: &'a mut BTreeMap<String, Queue>,
    now: u64,
    name: &str,
) -> Result<&'a mut Queue> {
    let queue = queues.get_mut(name).ok_or_else(|| does_not_exist(name))?;
    queue.expire(now);
    Ok(queue)
}

fn does_not_exist(name: &str) -> Error {
    Error::new(
        ErrorCode::QueueDoesNotExist,
        format!("queue `{name}` does not exist"),
    )
}

/// Builds a result member map from name/value pairs.
fn members<const N: usize>(pairs: [(&str, Value); N]) -> Members {
    pairs.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_owned(), v)).collect()
}

//! Character and name rules shared by queue names and message identifiers.

const FIFO_SUFFIX: &str = ".fifo";
const MAX_QUEUE_NAME_LEN: usize = 80;

fn is_name_char(c: char) -> bool {
    c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '-'
}

/// True if `s` is made of 1 to `max_len` characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`.
pub fn is_identifier(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> bool {
    (1..=max_len).contains(&s.chars().count()) && s.chars().all(is_name_char)
}

/// True if `name` follows the queue name syntax (SPEC section 4).
pub fn is_valid_queue_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    match name.strip_suffix(FIFO_SUFFIX) {
        Some(stem) => is_identifier(stem, MAX_QUEUE_NAME_LEN - FIFO_SUFFIX.len()),
        None => is_identifier(name, MAX_QUEUE_NAME_LEN),
    }
}

/// True if the name denotes a FIFO queue by its suffix.
pub fn has_fifo_suffix(name: &str) -> bool {
    name.ends_with(FIFO_SUFFIX)
}

//! Parsing of command lines and typed access to their parameters.
//!
//! Parameter access follows the check order of SPEC section 2: a handler
//! first calls [`Params::require`] for all required names, then reads each
//! value with a typed getter, which reports `InvalidParameterValue`.

use std::ops::RangeInclusive;

use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::error::{Error, ErrorCode, Result};
use crate::naming;

/// A parsed command line: the command name and its parameter object.
pub struct Request {
    pub command: String,
    pub members: Map<String, Value>,
}

impl Request {
    /// Checks the request shape (SPEC section 2, check 1).
    pub fn parse(line: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
        let invalid = |msg: &str| Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, msg);
        let text = std::str::from_utf8(line).map_err(|_| invalid("line is not valid UTF-8"))?;
        let value: Value =
            serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| invalid(&format!("invalid JSON: {e}")))?;
        let Value::Object(members) = value else {
            return Err(invalid("request is not a JSON object"));
        };
        let command = match members.get("Command") {
            Some(Value::String(name)) => name.clone(),
            _ => return Err(invalid("`Command` is missing or not a string")),
        };
        Ok(Self { command, members })
    }

    pub fn params(&self) -> Params<'_> {
        Params::new(&self.members)
    }
}

/// Read-only typed view of a JSON object. `null` members count as absent.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Params<'a> {
    members: &'a Map<String, Value>,
}

fn invalid_value(name: &str, expected: &str) -> Error {
    Error::new(
        ErrorCode::InvalidParameterValue,
        format!("`{name}` must be {expected}"),
    )
}

impl<'a> Params<'a> {
    pub fn new(members: &'a Map<String, Value>) -> Self {
        Self { members }
    }

    fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
        self.members.get(name).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
    }

    pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.get(name).is_some()
    }

    /// Fails with `MissingParameter` for the first absent name.
    pub fn require(&self, names: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
        match names.iter().find(|name| !self.has(name)) {
            Some(name) => Err(Error::new(
                ErrorCode::MissingParameter,
                format!("`{name}` is required"),
            )),
            None => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    pub fn string(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a str>> {
        self.get(name)
            .map(|v| v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "a string")))
            .transpose()
    }

    pub fn boolean(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<bool>> {
        self.get(name)
            .map(|v| v.as_bool().ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "a boolean")))
            .transpose()
    }

66	## 4. Queues and messages

78	| `DeadLetterQueue` | string | any string (see the command rules) | unset |

90	
91	- *delayed*: it was sent at time `t` with delay `d`, and `now < t + d`;
92	- *in flight*: its latest delivery was at time `t` with visibility timeout `v`, and `now < t + v`;

94	
95	Retention: a message is removed for good as soon as `now >= SentAt + RetentionSeconds` of the queue that
96	holds it, whatever its state. This holds at every moment, so lowering `RetentionSeconds` can remove
97	messages at once, and raising it later does not bring them back.

172	from `t + 300` on, the next send with this id is accepted and opens a new window. Deduplication ids are
173	per queue, ignore `GroupId`, and outlive the original message: deleting it, or it leaving the queue in
174	any other way, does not free the id.
175	
176	**ReceiveMessage.** Parameters: `QueueName` (string, required); `MaxMessages` (integer, optional, 1 to
177	10, default 1); `VisibilityTimeout` (integer, optional, 0 to 43200, default: the queue's attribute).
178	
179	The messages of the queue are examined once each, in arrival order, until `MaxMessages` messages have
180	been delivered or the end of the queue is reached. A message is *eligible* if it is visible and, in a
181	FIFO queue, no earlier message with the same `GroupId` is still in the queue (in any state). Messages
182	that are not eligible are skipped. For each eligible message:
183	
184	- if the queue has a dead-letter configuration and the message's `ReceiveCount` is at least
185	  `MaxReceiveCount`, the message is moved to the dead-letter queue (below) instead of being delivered.
186	  It does not count toward `MaxMessages`, and the examination goes on;
187	- otherwise it is delivered: `ReceiveCount` grows by 1, `FirstReceivedAt` becomes `now` if it was unset,
188	  the message gets the next `ReceiptHandle`, and with visibility timeout `v` it is in flight while
189	  `now < (time of this delivery) + v`.
190	
191	Result: `Messages`, an array (possibly empty) in delivery order of objects with `MessageId`,
192	`ReceiptHandle`, `Body`, `ReceiveCount`, `SentAt`, `FirstReceivedAt` and, on a FIFO queue, `GroupId` and
193	`SequenceNumber`.
194	
195	Consequences: a message whose visibility timeout ends keeps its place in arrival order. With a
196	visibility timeout of 0 the message is visible again at once and its handle is never usable. One
197	`ReceiveMessage` on a FIFO queue delivers at most one message per group, and none from a group whose
198	earliest message is in flight or delayed.
199	
200	Dead-letter move: the message leaves its queue and is added at the end of the dead-letter queue. It
201	keeps `MessageId`, `Body`, `SentAt` and `GroupId`. Its `ReceiveCount` is 0 again, `FirstReceivedAt` is
202	unset, it has no delay (it is visible at once), and in a FIFO queue it takes the next `SequenceNumber`
203	of the dead-letter queue. The move neither checks nor records deduplication ids and ignores the message
204	limit. Retention keeps counting from `SentAt`, now under the dead-letter queue's `RetentionSeconds`, so
205	a message that is already too old there is removed on arrival.
206	
207	**DeleteMessage** and **ChangeMessageVisibility.** Parameters of both: `QueueName` and `ReceiptHandle`
208	(strings, required). `ChangeMessageVisibility` also takes `VisibilityTimeout` (integer, required, 0 to
209	43200).
210	
211	1. `ReceiptHandle` is not a handle that this process has issued so far: `ReceiptHandleInvalid`. Handles
212	   are compared as exact strings: `r-01`, `R-1` and `r-1 ` were never issued.
213	2. The handle is not the latest handle of a message that is in flight in this queue right now:
214	   `ReceiptHandleExpired`. This covers a message delivered again since, a visibility timeout that has
215	   ended, a message that is gone (deleted, purged, expired, moved to a dead-letter queue), and a handle
216	   issued for a message of another queue.
217	
218	`DeleteMessage` removes the message. `ChangeMessageVisibility` replaces the end of the message's
219	visibility timeout: it is now in flight while `now < (time of this command) + VisibilityTimeout`, so 0
220	makes it visible at once. Neither changes `ReceiveCount`. Result members: none.

626	impl Request {
627	    /// Checks the request shape (SPEC section 2, check 1).
628	    pub fn parse(line: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
629	        let invalid = |msg: &str| Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidRequest, msg);
630	        let text = std::str::from_utf8(line).map_err(|_| invalid("line is not valid UTF-8"))?;

633	        let Value::Object(members) = value else {
634	            return Err(invalid("request is not a JSON object"));
635	        };

637	            Some(Value::String(name)) => name.clone(),

652	}

654	fn invalid_value(name: &str, expected: &str) -> Error {
655	    Error::new(
656	        ErrorCode::InvalidParameterValue,

658	    )

661	impl<'a> Params<'a> {
662	    pub fn new(members: &'a Map<String, Value>) -> Self {
663	        Self { members }
664	    }

666	    fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
667	        self.members.get(name).filter(|v| !v.is_null())
668	    }
669	
670	    pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
671	        self.get(name).is_some()
672	    }

674	    /// Fails with `MissingParameter` for the first absent name.
675	    pub fn require(&self, names: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
676	        match names.iter().find(|name| !self.has(name)) {
677	            Some(name) => Err(Error::new(
678	                ErrorCode::MissingParameter,
679	                format!("`{name}` is required"),
680	            )),
681	            None => Ok(()),
682	        }
683	    }

685	    pub fn string(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a str>> {
686	        self.get(name)
687	            .map(|v| v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "a string")))
688	            .transpose()
689	    }

691	    pub fn boolean(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<bool>> {
692	        self.get(name)
693	            .map(|v| v.as_bool().ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "a boolean")))
694	            .transpose()
695	    }

697	    /// An integer written without fraction or exponent, within `range`.
698	    pub fn integer(&self, name: &str, range: RangeInclusive<u64>) -> Result<Option<u64>> {
699	        let Some(value) = self.get(name) else {
700	            return Ok(None);
701	        };
702	        let number = value
703	            .as_number()
704	            .and_then(|n| n.as_i64())
705	            .ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "an integer"))?;
706	        u64::try_from(number)
707	            .ok()
708	            .filter(|n| range.contains(n))
709	            .map(Some)
710	            .ok_or_else(|| {
711	                invalid_value(
712	                    name,
713	                    &format!("between {} and {}", range.start(), range.end()),
714	                )
715	            })
716	    }

718	    /// A string of 1 to `max_len` characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`.
719	    pub fn identifier(&self, name: &str, max_len: usize) -> Result<Option<&'a str>> {
720	        match self.string(name)? {
721	            Some(s) if !naming::is_identifier(s, max_len) => Err(invalid_value(
722	                name,
723	                &format!("1 to {max_len} characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -"),
724	            )),
725	            other => Ok(other),
726	        }
727	    }

729	    pub fn object(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<Params<'a>>> {
730	        self.get(name)
731	            .map(|v| {
732	                v.as_object()
733	                    .map(Params::new)
734	                    .ok_or_else(|| invalid_value(name, "an object"))
735	            })
736	            .transpose()
737	    }

739	    /// Fails with `InvalidParameterValue` if a member is not in `known`.
740	    pub fn reject_unknown(&self, known: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
741	        match self.members.keys().find(|k| !known.contains(&k.as_str())) {
742	            Some(key) => Err(Error::new(
743	                ErrorCode::InvalidParameterValue,
744	                format!("unknown attribute `{key}`"),
745	            )),
746	            None => Ok(()),
747	        }
748	    }

content.text:
I added all three features from `SPEC-feature.md`, one commit each. `cargo test` passes with the new tests, and clippy reports nothing.

- **`MaxMessageBytes`:**
  - It is a new queue attribute, 1 to 1024 with a default of 1024.
  - `SendMessage` now rejects a body longer than the queue's limit, after the queue lookup and before its other rules.
  - One existing test, `create_uses_defaults` in `tests/queues.rs`, asserts the exact attribute set. I added `MaxMessageBytes` to its expected value, because the new spec makes `GetQueueAttributes` return it always.
- **Queue tags:** `TagQueue`, `UntagQueue` and `ListQueueTags`, with the key, value and 50-tag limits from the spec. Tags sit apart from the attributes, so `CreateQueue` equality, `GetQueueAttributes` and `PurgeQueue` ignore them. `DeleteQueue` removes them with the queue.
- **Batches:**
  - `SendMessageBatch` and `DeleteMessageBatch` return `Successful` and `Failed` arrays.
  - They share code with the single commands rather than copying the rules. I split `SendMessage` into parameter parsing and the queue-side rules, and `DeleteMessage` into a reusable handle deletion.
  - The four new error codes are added.

I put `to_json` on the error type so failure responses and failed batch entries build the error object in one place.

The new tests are in `tests/batches.rs` and `tests/tags.rs`, plus additions to `tests/queues.rs` and `tests/messages.rs`. They cover rule order, per-entry failures, deduplication and sequence numbers inside a batch, and the 100000-message limit hit in the middle of a batch.
